name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Brian Babin running with a large cash advantage
Democratic challenger Rhonda Hart has raised no money
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 6%
model.rationale: Babin holds a deep-red R+12 seat, has roughly $900k on hand, and faces a challenger with no fundraising, while markets price his reelection around 93%. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Republican win.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting the seat would be the first sign the race is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brian Babin seeks another term in a southeast Texas district that leans heavily Republican, about twelve points toward the GOP at the baseline. He enters the general election with a strong financial position, having raised over a million dollars and holding roughly $900,000 on hand.

His Democratic opponent, Rhonda Hart, has reported no fundraising and no cash on hand, leaving her little ability to compete in a media market. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Babin about a 93% chance of winning. All available evidence points to a safe Republican hold with a margin in the mid-teens.
